deprecations.title: PSF Guard is moving to its own catalogs
deprecations.body:
For new Target Scheduler databases, choose Settings → Databases → Import from Target Scheduler to import the database and set up sync.

Your current Target Scheduler setup will keep working in 0.12. A later update will create a PSF Guard catalog for you and keep captures, plans and grades in sync with Target Scheduler.

Separate catalogs let us add features to PSF Guard and support new Target Scheduler versions. We plan to remove direct database access in 0.13 or later.

upgradeNotes.title: Choose how Target Scheduler syncs
upgradeNotes.body: New Target Scheduler connections create a PSF Guard-owned catalog. Local-file imports enable automatic sync and grade writeback; review the startup, change detection and schedule settings after importing. Grade writeback has its own switch. Manual planning and grade transfers use Preview and Apply. Director activation sends approved planning through the saved TS connection and retries failed deliveries.

upgradeNotes.title: Allow time for calibration checks and rebuilds
upgradeNotes.body: The first start reads frame sites, grades calibration frames and measures flat groups in the background. Stacks and masters rebuild once when you next use them. PSF Guard does not reuse plate solves or satellite predictions made by 0.11, so it solves frames again. Work you start takes priority over these checks.

upgradeNotes.title: Review new targets and planning changes
upgradeNotes.body: Automatic image-folder import now holds frames for unknown targets for Review. Change New targets in the database settings to create projects automatically. Before activating a plan, check its preview: activation turns off exposure plans the plan does not include. Take Target Scheduler’s values keeps plans made in N.I.N.A.

upgradeNotes.title: Keep a copy of settings before a downgrade
upgradeNotes.body: PSF Guard 0.11 can open catalogs graded by 0.12, but it ignores the new calibration grades and choices apart from darks graded for stray light. Saving settings in an older version drops the new calibration settings and rig overrides.

highlights.title: Keep your catalog separate from Target Scheduler
highlights.body: Import a local Target Scheduler file into a PSF Guard-owned catalog, or pair the PSF Guard Sync plugin without a local TS file. Capture imports keep local grades and measurements. Grade writeback reports conflicts instead of overwriting TS edits. You can also import a standalone catalog copy or choose its storage path.

highlights.title: Inspect calibration frames and masters
highlights.body: The Calibration page shows each frame’s grade, the inputs to each master and the projects they serve. Keep a frame out, use it anyway, compare it with its session, or repair duplicate records without deleting files.

highlights.title: Match flats by what they measure
highlights.body: Group flats across nights by their measured pattern and dust changes. Inspect disks, donuts and vignetting, split or join groups, and choose which side of a change supplies a light’s flats.

highlights.title: Stretch stacks and calibrate colour with Gaia
highlights.body: Median anchor and Layered stretches join Auto MTF, which stays the default. Install Gaia colors in Settings › Catalogs to calibrate RGB, LRGB and one-shot-colour stacks against star colours. Stacks keep their processing when they rebuild.

highlights.title: Keep stacks through engine updates
highlights.body: From 0.12 on, Seiza updates that leave stacking output unchanged reuse completed stacks and calibration masters. If only the display stretch or one-shot-color calibration is out of date, Build current set refreshes the card preview from the saved FITS. The stack, processing and downloads stay available. Queued previews show Waiting to render preview on the card and in the job list.

highlights.title: Combine WBPP masters in color
highlights.body: Combine channel stacks gives WBPP masters their own card, including projects split by exposure. Source labels show the sub-exposure when known. Use Custom combination to choose between several masters of one filter or to mix WBPP and PSF Guard sources.

highlights.title: Adjust color while stacks build
highlights.body: Changes to a color card's stretch, calibration or crop can run alongside stack builds when they reuse prepared channels. Compositions you start that need no deconvolution or RC-Astro can also run this way, unless another composition is preparing the same uncached inputs. After a build you start, each target's color can compose once its own channels finish. Other color work stays in the build queue.

highlights.title: Plan mosaics across rigs
highlights.body: Place and turn panels one at a time, keep panels already shot in place, and frame rigs separately. Activation previews show what each rig will shoot, and a site that missed an activation can receive it again. Planning explains why a catalog is unavailable and offers Retry planning. With Snap on, a panel dragged along its row stays in that row beside diagonal neighbours.

highlights.title: Back up now or on a schedule
highlights.body: Back up settings, accounts, plans and catalogs to one archive. Download it in a browser, save it to a folder, or schedule daily or weekly backups with retention limits. Settings keeps the last result after a restart.

highlights.title: Review images on a laptop or phone
highlights.body: Browse by each rig’s observing night, show newest frames first and select Sequence frames by score, stars or HFR. View choices follow signed-in accounts. A smaller phone header and grading bar leave more room for images.

highlights.title: Resize the desktop UI
highlights.body: Choose Zoom in, Zoom out or Reset to 100% from the menu. Cmd/Ctrl with +, − or 0 changes the whole UI from 50% to 200%, including Settings. The app remembers the scale on this device; image zoom stays separate.

highlights.title: Follow and stop background work
highlights.body: The jobs list shows progress for previews, imports, exports, calibration checks and catalog upkeep as well as stacks. Stop an import to roll it back, or stop an export and keep completed files. Quality scans you start queue behind the current scan and run before database-wide analysis. Builds you start pause automatic builds, which resume from their checkpoints.

highlights.title: Clearer help and status messages
highlights.body: Import settings, satellite results, planning help and collaboration messages explain what PSF Guard does and what you can do next. The import preview explains that Skip processed files also skips calibrated and registered copies when pairing is off.

highlights.title: Scroll through server information
highlights.body: Server information scrolls its database list while its heading and close controls stay visible. Database IDs, files and image folders have separate labels; long paths wrap. Server details and the database list have separate loading and error messages. Retry reloads only the failed request.

highlights.title: Load the current UI after signing in
highlights.body: Successful browser sign-ins reload the current URL to load the server's current UI after an update. PSF Guard checks that the session was saved before reloading. Failed sign-ins stay on the login form.

highlights.title: Keep Sequence charts in view
highlights.body: The summary, suspect pills and score chart stay below the toolbar while you browse frames. On short windows, they scroll with the page to leave room for frames. Click a Solved pointing point, or focus it and press Enter, to move to its frame without changing your selection. Collapse the chart from its heading; PSF Guard remembers the choice in this browser.

highlights.title: Start stack builds without waiting for preparation
highlights.body: Build stacks, Build current set and Build on a channel card appear immediately as Preparing stack build. PSF Guard prepares the frames in the background and then queues one build per channel. You can stop preparation before channel builds are queued. Requests keep their queue position after a restart, including during preparation. Calibration checks and exports also start sooner by reading the library once per request.

highlights.title: Process each channel after its build
highlights.body: With Re-apply processing when a stack refreshes on, each channel’s saved processing runs after a build you start or take over, ahead of your other queued builds. Processing after automatic refreshes waits behind your work and builds of the same target. Card previews refreshed after an engine update appear as soon as the refresh finishes.

highlights.title: Stack frames at different rotator angles
highlights.body: Chosen by Seiza selects a reference from the largest orientation group, so a small group does not cause most frames to fail the rotation check. Adjust Orientation group margin in Settings → Stacking. If grading leaves fewer than two usable frames, the channel’s old stack is removed from its card and color source choices.

highlights.title: Queue color before channels finish
highlights.body: Start a color preview while its channels are preparing or building. It waits for them, uses their new stacks and survives a server restart. Queued builds and color previews read the latest frames, grades and calibration when they start.

highlights.title: Change a transfer preview while it runs
highlights.body: In Data Transfer and Remote PSF Guard, changing options stops the current preview. Preview the new choices immediately. A newer sync, import or export preview replaces one still running.

highlights.title: Follow and stop preview pre-generation
highlights.body: When preview pre-generation is enabled on the server, Generating previews shows progress for each database. Stop disables pre-generation for that database until the server restarts; previews you open still generate as needed. Pre-generation waits while your jobs run, then continues from where it paused.

upgradeNotes.title: Docker settings moved
upgradeNotes.body: Settings now live in /data/config/psf-guard and the cache in /data/cache. If you mounted /home/psfguard/.config, copy its psf-guard folder into /data/config/ before starting 0.11, or your databases and users will be missing.

upgradeNotes.title: Allow time for the first start
upgradeNotes.body: PSF Guard backs up each catalog and updates its calibration tables. A background pass then measures raw darks. Stacks, masters and colour composites rebuild once when you next use them.

upgradeNotes.title: Cache cleanup starts at 90% disk use
upgradeNotes.body: PSF Guard removes previews, checkpoints and unused masters it can rebuild. It never removes stacks. Change the limit in Settings › Storage. Read the full release notes before going back to 0.10.5.

highlights.title: Plan across rigs
highlights.body: Frame targets, set goals per filter and share the work between rigs. Preview each plan before writing it to Target Scheduler.

highlights.title: Build and review stacks in one place
highlights.body: Stacks has its own view, with noise-weighted builds, colour previews and WBPP runs.

highlights.title: Check calibration before stacking
highlights.body: Find lights your library cannot calibrate and keep darks with stray light out of masters.

highlights.title: Connect an agent
highlights.body: Let an MCP agent work with catalogs, plans and stacks within your account's access limits.
